end.summary:
Practised identifying standing, sleeping and slanting straight lines.
Classified straight and curved lines in examples including U, V and a bangle edge.
Answered 3 of 6 line-identification attempts without help and 2 of 2 straight-versus-curved attempts without help.
V was still described as curved because it has a corner; this was not corrected in a later response.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Om practised standing, sleeping, slanting, straight and curved lines using examples such as a kite string, slide and bangle. They used the direction and shape of a line to explain several answers, including that a slanting line can still be straight. Om mixed up a bent V with a curved line, and this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask them to sort drawn examples into straight-with-corners, curved, standing, sleeping and slanting groups, reminding them that corners do not make a line curved.
